**Finding resubmitted: Compliant (preferred position)** — no redline, paragraph returned unchanged.

The repair addressed the verifier's two failed deterministic checks directly in the rationale rather than changing the classification, since the verifier confirmed both failures are artifacts of there being no covenant to measure:

- **Duration ≤ 12 months** — no restricted period exists to cap.
- **General-solicitation carve-out** — no prohibition exists needing a carve-out; § 12.3 instead supplies the equivalent protection affirmatively, preserving our freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and recording that we have made "no ... no-hire commitment."

I also tightened the quote onto the operative no-hire/general-recruitment language so the cited text maps directly to the checks in question.

Net position: the agreement sits above our fallback (a narrowed mutual non-solicit) and squarely at the preferred position of no non-solicit binding Meridian Fieldworks. Two carry-forward notes for the deal team: § 12.3 is favourable drafting worth defending if Copperleaf proposes to trim it, and § 12.4's 24-month non-compete on us remains a live issue under the restrictive-covenant/exclusivity rule — including its direct contradiction of § 12.3's statement that we have made no non-compete commitment.
